- `base_grid` — same shape as `grid`; the map before any runtime edit. Replaying
  the change history against it must reproduce `grid`.
- `tick` — number of ticks already executed.
- `robots` — list of `{"robot_id", "position", "route", "task_id",
  "distance_travelled"}`; `position` is `[x, y]` and `route` is the remaining
  waypoints after the current position (empty for a paused robot).
- `tasks` — list of `{"task_id", "pickup", "dropoff", "assigned_robot",
  "picked_up", "completed"}`. Completed tasks keep their historical
  `assigned_robot`; unassigned tasks use `null`.
- `paused_tasks` — ids of tasks whose assigned robot currently cannot reach a
  required point on the saved map.
- `traffic_waits` — optional list of `{"robot_id", "blocked_by", "ticks"}`
  entries: robots currently held up by other robots, who blocks them, and for
  how many consecutive ticks. Older files without this field load with every
  counter at zero.
- `map_changes` — every actual edit in order, each
  `{"tick", "sequence", "added", "removed"}`; `sequence` runs from 1 and
  consecutive edits at the same `tick` preserve their order.
- `replay` — ordered events. Tick frames are `{"type": "tick", "tick", "moved",
  "robots", "completed"}`, numbered consecutively from `1` through `tick`.
  Map-change frames are interspersed at their effective tick and have the shape
  `{"type": "map_change", "tick", "sequence", "added", "removed"}`. In any
  non-zero-tick file the last tick frame's robot positions must equal the
  current robot positions; historical frames are never overwritten by later
  maps.

Loading validates the entire document: corrupted JSON, missing or wrongly
typed fields, unsupported versions, duplicate robot or task ids, overlapping
or out-of-bounds/blocked robot positions, routes that leave the map, cross
obstacles, make non-adjacent moves, or cannot complete the robot's bound task,
task/robot ownership mismatches, a broken replay history, out-of-bounds or
add/remove-conflicting change records,
a change history that does not reproduce the saved grid, and an inconsistent
paused-task state are all rejected. So is a replay whose *history* could never
have happened, even when its final frame matches the saved robots: a robot out
of bounds or on an obstacle that existed at that tick, two robots sharing a
cell at a tick boundary, a jump of more than one orthogonal cell or a two-robot
cell swap between neighboring tick frames, and a `moved` list that names an
unknown/duplicated robot or does not exactly match the robots that changed
position (following another robot into the cell it just vacated is legal, and
the list need not be sorted). Map edits are judged against contemporary
positions: a cell a robot once passed through may be closed later without
invalidating the replay, a robot may not appear in a cell before it opens, and
an edit may not add an obstacle onto a cell occupied when that tick ended —
not even if another edit of the same tick removes it again. The first tick
frame has no recorded predecessor, so its cells, overlaps and `moved` ids are
still checked but the first moves are not second-guessed; zero-tick files,
empty fleets and all-waiting frames remain valid. Beyond physical
plausibility, each assigned, unfinished, non-paused task must still be
completable along its robot's remaining route: a non-empty route has to end at
the dropoff, and a robot that has not collected yet — unless it is already
standing on the pickup cell — must still pass through the pickup (visiting the
dropoff early and leaving again is fine; detours need not match a replanned
shortest path). An empty route is accepted only for a loaded robot already at
the dropoff, or when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; map-paused
tasks keep their empty-route exemption. Version 1 documents contain
tick frames without a `type` field and none of the edit-related keys; they
load as if no map edit had ever happened.

1	"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.
2	
3	Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
4	:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
5	deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
6	event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
7	never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
8	information recorded at the time.
9	
10	Automatic yielding
11	------------------
12	When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
13	keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: an idle blocker is asked to
14	move onto a free side cell that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy
15	robot facing a blocker that cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free
16	adjacent cell and replan its (still shortest) route from there. A retreat that
17	only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
18	replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
19	blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
20	corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
21	empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Yield moves count as
22	mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
23	completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
24	takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
25	time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
26	purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
27	blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
28	:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
29	map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
30	end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
31	asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
32	made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
33	and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
34	tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
35	blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
36	identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
37	interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
38	reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
39	longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
40	entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
41	or increments one.
42	
43	Checkpoint file format
44	----------------------
45	``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
46	version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.
47	
48	``version``
49	    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
50	``grid``
51	    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
52	    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
53	``tick``
54	    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
55	    loading never advance this value.
56	``robots``
57	    List of robot states, each
58	    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
59	    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
60	    remaining waypoints after ``position``.
61	``tasks``
62	    List of task states, each
63	    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
64	    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
65	    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``.
66	``replay``
67	    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
68	    through ``tick`` and have the shape
69	    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
70	    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
71	    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
72	    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
73	    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
74	    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
75	    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
76	    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
77	    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
78	    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
79	    robot positions.
80	``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
81	    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
82	    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
83	``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
84	    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
85	    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
86	    ``grid``.
87	``traffic_waits`` (optional)
88	    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
89	    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
90	    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
91	    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
92	    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
93	    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
94	    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
95	    all reject the document.
96	
97	Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
98	``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
99	baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.
100	
101	Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
102	fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
103	bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
104	mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
105	that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
106	or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
107	states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
108	:class:`ValueError`.
109	
110	A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
111	walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
112	unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
113	the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
114	pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
115	dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
116	and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
117	route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
118	when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
119	empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.
120	
121	The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
122	for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
123	cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
124	robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
125	may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
126	cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
127	fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
128	duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
129	robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
130	applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
131	robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
132	cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
133	frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
134	it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
135	"""

154	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
155	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
156	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

159	def _as_cell(value: object, description: str) -> Position:
160	    """Validate a user supplied coordinate as a two-integer pair."""
161	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
162	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
163	    if len(value) != 2:
164	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
165	    if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
166	        raise ValueError(f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types")
167	    return value[0], value[1]
168

170	def _as_pair(value: object, description: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
171	    if (
172	        not isinstance(value, list)
173	        or len(value) != 2
174	        or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
175	    ):
176	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
177	    return value[0], value[1]

180	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
181	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
182	
183	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
184	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
185	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
186	
187	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
188	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
189	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
190	      completes anything by itself.
191	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
192	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
193	
194	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
195	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
196	    unreachable one.
197	    """
198	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
199	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
200	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
201	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
202	    if task.dropoff != last:
203	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
204	    return waypoints
205	
206	
207	def _plan_task_route(
208	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
209	) -> list[Position] | None:
210	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
211	
212	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
213	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
214	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
215	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
216	    """
217	    route: list[Position] = []
218	    current = origin
219	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
220	        try:
221	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
222	        except ValueError:
223	            return None
224	        route.extend(leg)
225	        current = waypoint
226	    return route

229	class FleetSimulator:
230	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
231	        self.grid = grid
232	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
233	        # replayed against this baseline.
234	        self.base_grid = grid
235	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
236	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
237	        self.tick = 0
238	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
239	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
240	        self._map_sequence = 0
241	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
242	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
243	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
244	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
245	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
246	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
247	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
248	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
249	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
250	
251	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
252	    # Dynamic map edits
253	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
254	
255	    def modify_obstacles(
256	        self,
257	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
258	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
259	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
260	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
261	
262	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
263	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
264	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
265	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
266	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
267	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
268	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
269	
270	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
271	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
272	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
273	        distance is accumulated.
274	        """
275	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
276	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
277	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
278	        if conflict:
279	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
280	            raise ValueError(
281	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
282	            )
283	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
284	        for cell in add_cells:
285	            if cell in occupied:
286	                raise ValueError(
287	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
288	                )
289	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
290	
291	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
292	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
293	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
294	        seen: set[Position] = set()
295	        ordered: list[Position] = []
296	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
297	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
298	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
299	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
300	            if position in seen:
301	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
302	                continue
303	            seen.add(position)
304	            ordered.append(position)
305	        return ordered
306	
307	    def _apply_map_change(
308	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
309	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
310	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
311	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
312	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
313	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
314	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
315	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
316	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
317	
318	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
319	        # known to change the map.
320	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
321	        self._map_sequence += 1
322	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
323	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
324	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
325	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
326	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
327	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
328	
329	    def _map_change_record(
330	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
331	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
332	        return {
333	            "type": "map_change",
334	            "tick": self.tick,
335	            "sequence": sequence,
336	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
337	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
338	        }
339	
340	    def _plan_route(
341	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
342	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
343	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
344	
345	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
346	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
347	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
348	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
349	        """
350	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
351	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
352	
353	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
354	        for task in self.tasks.values():
355	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
356	                continue
357	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
358	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
359	                continue
360	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
361	            if route is None:
362	                robot.route = []
363	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
364	            else:
365	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
366	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
367	                robot.route = route
368	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
369	
370	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
371	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
372	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
373	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
374	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
375	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
376	                continue
377	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
378	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
379	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
380	                continue
381	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
382	            if route is None:
383	                robot.route = []
384	                continue
385	            robot.route = route
386	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
387	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
388	
389	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
390	    # Traffic conflicts and yielding
391	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
392	
393	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
394	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
395	        cells: set[Position] = set()
396	        for robot in self.robots.values():
397	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
398	                cells.update(robot.route)
399	        return cells
400	
401	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
402	        self,
403	        blocker: Robot,
404	        requester: Robot,
405	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
406	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
407	    ) -> Position | None:
408	        """Free side-cell an idle blocker can yield to, or None.
409	
410	        The target may not be the requester's own cell (that would swap the
411	        two robots within one tick) nor any cell another robot still plans to
412	        drive through, so the blocker never trades one blockage for another.
413	        """
414	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
415	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
416	            if cell == requester.position:
417	                continue
418	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
419	                continue
420	            if cell in on_routes:
421	                continue
422	            return cell
423	        return None
424	
425	    def _self_sidestep(
426	        self,
427	        robot: Robot,
428	        task: Task | None,
429	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
430	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
431	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
432	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
433	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
434	
435	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
436	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
437	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
438	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
439	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
440	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
441	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
442	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
443	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
444	        """
445	        if task is None or task.completed:
446	            return None
447	        destination = robot.route[0]
448	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
449	        if blocker_id is None:
450	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
451	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id)
452	        best: tuple[int, int, Position, list[Position]] | None = None
453	        for index, cell in enumerate(self.grid.neighbors(robot.position)):
454	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved or cell in on_routes:
455	                continue
456	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
457	            if route is None:
458	                continue
459	            if (
460	                blocker_id is not None
461	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
462	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
463	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
464	                )
465	            ):
466	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
467	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
468	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
469	                continue
470	            if best is None or (len(route), index) < (best[0], best[1]):
471	                best = (len(route), index, cell, route)
472	        if best is None:
473	            return None
474	        return best[2], best[3]
475	
476	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
477	        self,
478	        robot: Robot,
479	        side: Position,
480	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
481	        blocker_id: str,
482	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
483	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
484	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
485	    ) -> bool:
486	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
487	
488	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
489	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
490	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
491	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
492	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
493	        never rejected here.
494	        """
495	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
496	            return False
497	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
498	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
499	            return False
500	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
501	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
502	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
503	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
504	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
505	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
506	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
507	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
508	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
509	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
510	        return not self._can_vacate(
511	            blocker,
512	            robot,
513	            hyp_occupied,
514	            reserved,
515	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
516	            blocked_path,
517	        )

519	    def _can_vacate(
520	        self,
521	        blocker: Robot,
522	        requester: Robot,
523	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
524	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
525	        checking: frozenset[str],
526	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
527	    ) -> bool:
528	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
529	
530	        An idle blocker leaves only by yielding onto a safe side cell for the
531	        requesting robot; a busy blocker leaves by driving onto its next
532	        waypoint (possibly following a chain of robots that all move this tick)
533	        or by sidestepping onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by
534	        map unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave
535	        check is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
536	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
537	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive back
538	        through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so such
539	        sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on the
540	        blocker's own route does).
541	        """
542	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
543	            return False
544	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
545	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
546	            return False
547	        if task is not None and not blocker.route:
548	            # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this tick;
549	            # it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
550	            return False
551	        if task is None:
552	            # Idle robots only ever move by yielding for a requester.
553	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
554	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
555	        if blocker.route:
556	            ahead = blocker.route[0]
557	            if (
558	                self.grid.traversable(ahead)
559	                and ahead not in occupied
560	                and ahead not in reserved
561	            ):
562	                return True
563	            occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
564	            if (
565	                occupant_id is not None
566	                and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
567	                and occupant_id not in checking
568	            ):
569	                # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
570	                # vacates its cell this same tick.
571	                if self._can_vacate(
572	                    self.robots[occupant_id],
573	                    requester,
574	                    occupied,
575	                    reserved,
576	                    checking | {blocker.robot_id},
577	                    blocked_path,
578	                ):
579	                    return True
580	        # Otherwise the blocker might sidestep onto a free side cell itself,
581	        # but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has to use.
582	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
583	        for side_cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
584	            if (
585	                side_cell in occupied
586	                or side_cell in reserved
587	                or side_cell in on_routes
588	                or side_cell in blocked_path
589	            ):
590	                continue
591	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
592	                return True
593	        return False
594	
595	    def _update_traffic_waits(
596	        self,
597	        waited: dict[str, str],
598	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
599	    ) -> None:
600	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
601	
602	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
603	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
604	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
605	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
606	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
607	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
608	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
609	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
610	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
611	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
612	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
613	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
614	        """
615	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
616	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
617	        for robot_id in waited:
618	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
619	                continue
620	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
621	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
622	                continue
623	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
624	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
625	                continue
626	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
627	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
628	                continue
629	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
630	            if entry is None:
631	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
632	            else:
633	                surviving[robot_id] = {
634	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
635	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
636	                }
637	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
638	
639	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
640	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
641	
642	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
643	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
644	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
645	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
646	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
647	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
648	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
649	        """
650	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
651	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
652	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
653	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
654	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
655	                continue
656	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
657	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
658	
659	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
660	        return [
661	            {
662	                "robot_id": robot_id,
663	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
664	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
665	            }
666	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
667	        ]

673	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
674	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
675	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
676	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
677	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
678	            for robot in self.robots.values():
679	                if not robot.idle:
680	                    continue
681	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
682	                if route is None:
683	                    continue
684	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
685	            if not choices:
686	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
687	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
688	                continue
689	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
690	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
691	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
692	            robot.route = route
693	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
694	
695	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
696	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
697	        for robot in self.robots.values():
698	            if robot.task_id is None:
699	                continue
700	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
701	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
702	                task.picked_up = True
703	
704	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
705	        self._confirm_pickups()
706	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
707	        self.assign_tasks()
708	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
709	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
710	        self._confirm_pickups()
711	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
712	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
713	        moved: list[str] = []
714	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
715	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
716	
717	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
718	            del occupied[robot.position]
719	            robot.position = destination
720	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
721	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
722	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
723	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
724	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
725	
726	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
727	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
728	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
729	                continue
730	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
731	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
732	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
733	                continue
734	            if not robot.route:
735	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
736	                continue
737	            destination = robot.route[0]
738	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
739	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
740	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
741	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
742	                    if route is None:
743	                        robot.route = []
744	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
745	                    else:
746	                        robot.route = route
747	                continue
748	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
749	            if blocker_id is None:
750	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
751	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
752	                relocate(robot, destination)
753	                robot.route.pop(0)
754	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
755	                continue
756	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
757	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
758	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
759	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
760	                if blocker.task_id is None:
761	                    # Idle blocker: ask it to yield onto a free side cell,
762	                    # then take over the cell it vacated.
763	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
764	                    if side is not None:
765	                        relocate(blocker, side)
766	                        relocate(robot, destination)
767	                        robot.route.pop(0)
768	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
769	                        continue
770	                elif blocker.route:
771	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
772	                    if (
773	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
774	                        and ahead not in occupied
775	                        and ahead not in reserved
776	                    ):
777	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
778	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
779	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
780	                        continue
781	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
782	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
783	            side = self._self_sidestep(
784	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
785	            )
786	            if side is not None:
787	                cell, route = side
788	                relocate(robot, cell)
789	                robot.route = route
790	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
791	                continue
792	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
793	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
794	        self.tick += 1
795	        event: dict[str, object] = {
796	            "type": "tick",
797	            "tick": self.tick,
798	            "moved": moved,
799	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
800	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
801	        }
802	        self.replay.append(event)
803	        return event
804	
805	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
806	        if robot.task_id is None:
807	            return
808	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
809	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
810	            return
811	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
812	            task.picked_up = True
813	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
814	            task.completed = True
815	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
816	            robot.task_id = None

823	            "tasks_completed": completed,
824	            "tasks_paused": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
825	            "completion_ratio": completed / len(self.tasks) if self.tasks else 1.0,
826	            "distance_total": sum(robot.distance_travelled for robot in self.robots.values()),
827	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),

858	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
859	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
860	
861	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
862	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
863	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
864	        raise :class:`OSError`.
865	        """
866	        document = {
867	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
868	            "grid": {
869	                "width": self.grid.width,
870	                "height": self.grid.height,
871	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
872	            },
873	            "base_grid": {
874	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
875	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
876	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
877	            },
878	            "tick": self.tick,
879	            "robots": [
880	                {
881	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
882	                    "position": list(robot.position),
883	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
884	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
885	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
886	                }
887	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
888	            ],
889	            "tasks": [
890	                {
891	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
892	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
893	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
894	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
895	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
896	                    "completed": task.completed,
897	                }
898	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
899	            ],
900	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
901	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
902	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
903	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
904	        }
905	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
906	
907	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
908	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
909	        try:
910	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
911	            try:
912	                handle.write(payload)
913	                handle.flush()
914	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
915	            finally:
916	                handle.close()
917	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
918	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
919	        except BaseException:
920	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
921	            try:
922	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
923	            except OSError:
924	                pass
925	            raise
926	
927	    @staticmethod
928	    def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
929	        try:
930	            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
931	        except OSError:
932	            return
933	        try:
934	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
935	        except OSError:
936	            pass
937	        finally:
938	            os.close(dir_fd)

940	    @classmethod
941	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
942	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
943	
944	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
945	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
946	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
947	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
948	        """
949	        try:
950	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
951	                text = handle.read()
952	        except OSError:
953	            raise
954	        try:
955	            data = json.loads(text)
956	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
957	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc
958	        return cls._from_checkpoint(data)
959	
960	    @classmethod
961	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
962	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
963	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
964	
965	        version = data.get("version")
966	        if not _is_int(version):
967	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
968	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
969	            raise ValueError(
970	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
971	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
972	            )
973	
974	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
975	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
976	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
977	
978	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
979	        paused: set[str] = set()
980	        if version == 1:
981	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
982	            base_grid = grid
983	        else:
984	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
985	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
986	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
987	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
988	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
989	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
990	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
991	
992	        robots: list[Robot] = []
993	        for record in robot_records:
994	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
995	            if not grid.traversable(position):
996	                raise ValueError(
997	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
998	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
999	                )
1000	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1001	            previous = position
1002	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
1003	                waypoint = _as_pair(
1004	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1005	                )
1006	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1007	                    raise ValueError(
1008	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1009	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1010	                    )
1011	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
1012	                    raise ValueError(
1013	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
1014	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
1015	                    )
1016	                route.append(waypoint)
1017	                previous = waypoint
1018	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1019	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1020	                raise ValueError(
1021	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1022	                    "non-negative integer"
1023	                )
1024	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1025	
1026	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1027	        for record in task_records:
1028	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1029	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1030	            tasks.append(
1031	                Task(
1032	                    record["task_id"],
1033	                    pickup,
1034	                    dropoff,
1035	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1036	                    record["picked_up"],
1037	                    record["completed"],
1038	                )
1039	            )
1040	
1041	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1042	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1043	
1044	        for robot in robots:
1045	            if robot.task_id is not None:
1046	                task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
1047	                if task is None:
1048	                    raise ValueError(
1049	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task {robot.task_id!r}"
1050	                    )
1051	                if task.completed:
1052	                    raise ValueError(
1053	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} that is "
